one_month_reasoning: Events in the window: ASML Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-14 (guide EUR 11.0-12.0B, GM 55-57%; consensus EUR 10.65 EPS on EUR 11.68B sales, inside the guide), TSMC Q3 results and capex commentary on 2026-10-15, Lam and KLA results in late October, and the FOMC on 2026-10-27/28 after the 2026-09-16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (CME FedWatch had a hike at the next meeting near a coin flip right after the decision; the supervisor cites Polymarket at ~60% no change for October, so a modest headwind, not a shock). The MATCH Act cannot be decided in the window: the Senate adjourned 2026-09-30 and returns the week of 2026-11-09, with a December conference text the realistic path (supervisor, CRS IN12704). Industry data into the print is strong: Micron (2026-09-30) sees FY27-28 supply much tighter, TrendForce has 4Q26 DRAM contract prices up 10-20%, brokers have TSMC 2027 capex at $77-85B, and Goldman/SEMI see WFE still growing in 2028. I expect a beat and constructive 2027 color, but bookings are no longer disclosed, and the stock has already rebounded ~15% from the $1,575.15 close on 2026-09-14, so much of that is priced in. No directional edge: lognormal with median ~$1,813 at ~13.5% monthly vol (46%/3.5, nudged up for the print), tails slightly fattened.

fair_value.method: 60% forward P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 = 0.25 x 2027E EUR 54 + 0.75 x 2028E EUR 60 = EUR 58.5 = ~$65.8 at EUR/USD 1.1243, x 28.5x = ~$1,875) and 40% FCF yield (2028E FCF/share ~EUR 55.7 = ~$62.6 at a 3.35% yield = ~$1,869), blended to ~$1,875 for the stock 12 months out.

Implied Q4 2026 run rate (~EUR 14.4B) annualizes to ~EUR 57B. Consensus EUR 54.6B (Yahoo and MarketScreener agree). Customer capex rising: TSMC 2027 capex $77-85B (Citi $77B, Goldman $78B), Micron FY27 capex higher, Samsung P5 (~20 EUV), SK hynix (~20 EUV through 2027). Slightly above consensus.

EUR 56.5B x ~57% GM = 32.2B; less opex ~6.9B = EBIT ~25.3B; ~17% tax = ~21.0B; / ~381M average shares (Q2-26 basic 384.5M per the 6-K statements, ~1%/yr buyback) = ~EUR 55, trimmed to 54 for opex and mix risk. Consensus EUR 51.73 (Yahoo) / 52.29 (MarketScreener), both EUR.

2028 sales ~EUR 63B (+12%, between SEMI's +14% 2028 equipment growth and a slowing 2028 hyperscaler capex path; Goldman's WFE +29% is the high end; consensus EUR 65.0B) x ~36% net margin = ~EUR 22.7B / ~377M shares = ~EUR 60.2, less ~1% for probability-weighted MATCH risk = ~EUR 60. Below MarketScreener's EUR 68.3, whose NI of EUR 24.4B implies only ~356M shares; on ~377M shares consensus is ~EUR 64.6.

Today ~31x CY2027 consensus (EUR 51.73 = $58.2) and ~33x blended NTM. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 with another hike possible, which argues for a de-rating; 2028 equipment spending still growing (SEMI +14%, Goldman WFE +29%) argues against a deep one. I cut from 29x to 28.5x.

inputs_detail.derivation: ~EUR 22.6B net income (2028E EPS x shares), ~93% cash conversion after capex for the Eindhoven campus and capacity expansion, partly offset by customer down-payments in a sold-out market
Basic weighted shares 385.4M in Q1 2026 and 384.5M in Q2 2026 (6-K statements; round 1 wrongly had ~382M). Buybacks retire ~1%/yr, giving ~378M at end-2027 and ~377M average for 2028.
A 28.5x P/E is a 3.5% earnings yield; times ~0.95 FCF conversion gives ~3.35%. Raised from 3.25% for the 2026-09-16 Fed hike.

bear.story: In 2027 markets start to treat the cycle as peaking. Hyperscaler capex growth slows sharply for 2028, memory prices roll over as Micron, SK hynix and Samsung fabs ramp in 2027-28, and 2028 EUV orders disappoint. A December NDAA conference enacts the MATCH Act's DUV sales and servicing ban at named Chinese fabs (China ~14% of Q2 system sales, ~20% for FY26). The Fed keeps hiking. NTM EPS gets cut to ~$56 and the multiple falls to ~21x.

base.story: 2027 sales ~EUR 56B on 80-85 EUV units, GM ~57%. The 2028 outlook is for further growth (SEMI +14% equipment) on EUV pricing and memory High-NA. NTM EPS ~$66-68 at ~29x.

bull.story: ASML confirms another +30% capacity step for 2028, like-for-like EUV price increases stick, TSMC 2027 capex comes in at $85B+, and 2028 WFE tracks Goldman's +29% rather than SEMI's +14%. MATCH stays stalled. NTM EPS ~$75 at ~34.5x (trimmed from 37x in round 1 because of the hiking Fed and peer post-run-up base rates).

thesis_break_reason: About 19x my NTM EPS at the horizon (~$65.8), ~20.5x 2027E (~$60.7), ~31% below today and roughly at the March-2026 low (~$1,248). The 2026-09-14 selloff to $1,575.15 close came on sentiment alone, so a sustained trade at $1,250 would most likely mean the 2027-28 growth case broke (EUV slots pushed out, a memory capex cut as prices roll over, a guidance cut at the January 2027 results, or a December NDAA that enacts the China DUV sales and servicing ban), not ordinary 46%-vol noise. I keep $1,250 rather than the supervisor's $1,200: my bear path ($1,175) assumes that kind of damage, so the break should sit above it.

reasoning: Revision round after the supervisor's review (7 more searches/fetches). The supervisor confirmed my EUR correction (2027 consensus EUR 51.73, ~31x) and flagged three things: the Fed's 2026-09-16 hike, missing from my multiple argument (I verified it: CNBC/Fox, 25bp to 3.75-4.00%, another hike possible); a Q2 share count of 384.5M, not ~382M; and a right tail that was the highest of the five. I acted on all three. P/E: I now capitalize NTM EPS at the horizon (EUR 58.5 = 0.25 x 2027E 54 + 0.75 x 2028E 60), not pure 2028 EPS, at 28.5x (down from 29x for rates), which gives $1,875. FCF: 2028E ~$62.6/share at 3.35% (up from 3.25%) gives $1,869. Fair value falls from $1,940 to ~$1,875. My 2028 EPS of EUR 60 sits below MarketScreener's 68.3, which implies ~356M shares; on ~377M shares consensus is ~EUR 64.6. I stay below it because industry 2028 growth forecasts are split: SEMI +14% for equipment, Goldman WFE +29%. Rather than copy consensus, I take ~EUR 63B of sales at ~36% net margin. On the bull case: the supervisor asked me to justify 37x under a hiking Fed and peer base rates (AMAT fell 1-38% after similar run-ups). I can't fully justify it, so I trimmed the bull to $2,600 at ~34.5x with 23% probability, and the bear to $1,175 / 23% (Fed plus a December MATCH path). The scenario mean is ~$1,920. Ladder: lognormal with median ~$1,870 (close to my $1,875 fair value, a little below the ~$1,920 scenario mean), sigma 0.39 above and 0.46 below (a fatter left tail for cycle and policy shocks), below the 46% realized vol, which the 2025-26 re-rating inflated. P(>=spot) goes from 0.555 to 0.53, P(>=2713) from 0.21 to 0.17 and P(>=4521) from 0.022 to 0.014. I keep the thesis break at $1,250 rather than $1,200 (see reason). Limits: X was not used, the SEMI site returned 403 (I used Semiconductor Digest's restatement), and I found no liquid prediction market on the MATCH Act.
